or_d_aggro_gully.blurb: Aggro Gully is a steep, narrow gully at Smith Rock tucked between the East and West Ship formations, and it holds some of the park's most overhanging sport climbing. The routes are single-pitch and bolted, with the bulk of them in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, plus a short run of low-5.11 and 5.10 lines and several 5.14s at the top end. Expect sustained, pumpy climbing rather than slabby footwork. The gully tends to give shade in the heat of summer and catches sun on cold days, which makes it a useful stop in more than one season. It sits a short walk above the river trail.
or_d_aggro_gully.approach: Cross the footbridge and head along the river path a few minutes; the first steep stair-stepped trail climbing up on the left leads into the gully.

or_greensprings.blurb: Greensprings is a small cluster of rock columns in the hills above Emigrant Lake, east of Ashland, with edges, knobs and sloping holds on the faces. Climbs run up to roughly 100 feet and mix bolted lines with traditional ones, so a rack is useful for part of it. Grades start low but most of the climbing sits around 5.10 and 5.11, and some of the harder, less-traveled routes can be mossy. The columns pick up afternoon sun, which suits cold-weather days and turns hot in summer. Loose scree sits on the ledges above, so keep helmets on and watch who is standing below. The crag is on private land, so be tidy and courteous.
or_greensprings.parking_note: Turn off the highway onto Tyler Creek Road and follow it downhill a short way to a roadside pullout. The trail begins from there and is steep with loose gravel, so sturdy shoes help.

_expect.name: Meadow Camp, AKA Meadow Picnic Area

or_meadow_camp_aka_meadow_picnic_area.blurb: Meadow Camp is a bouldering area beside the Deschutes River on the Cascade Lakes Highway just outside Bend. The volcanic rock offers pockets, crimps and some cracks, and it can be hard on the skin. Problems range from short, friendly boulders to taller ones that call for a confident spotter or extra pads, and the grades cover everything from the easiest to the hard end of the V-scale, with most of them in the V1 to V6 range. The setting is quiet and wooded, with the river running close by, and the boulders are spread along the water so walks vary from a couple of minutes to much longer depending on which one you want.
or_meadow_camp_aka_meadow_picnic_area.parking_note: Drive out the highway and turn left on the gravel road just before the golf course. Leave your car in the first lot next to the river and walk downstream toward the boulders.

or_kangaroo_the.blurb: The Kangaroo is a thick, tall spire in the Marsupials, the remote eastern corner of Smith Rock, and it sees far fewer climbers than the main canyon. Nearly all the lines are bolted sport routes, and the focus is steep, powerful climbing: most of the grades fall in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with only a few easier ones. A lot of the sport climbing is on the west side of the formation. Getting here takes a long walk from the main lot, so bring water, plan for a full day and expect solitude. Rock quality varies, and some of the newer routes may still have loose bits.

or_mile_marker_5.blurb: Mile Marker 5 is a small roadside bouldering area on Skyliners Road, a short drive up from Bend. The boulders sit in the trees and stay shaded, which makes them a good choice on hot days. Problems span the full range from VB to V7, with a nice cluster in the V0 to V4 range, and the landings are generally flat. Individual blocks and walls such as the Left Wall, Right Wall and Overhang Boulder keep a session of an hour or two varied. The walk from the car is brief and the trail is easy to follow.
or_mile_marker_5.parking_note: Take Skyliners Road about five miles out of town. The boulders come into view around a wide left bend; a small log-edged pullout on the left holds a few cars, with a short trail to the rock.

or_hardscrabble_wall.blurb: Hardscrabble Wall is the right-hand section of Madrone Wall, a basalt cliff above the Clackamas River southeast of Portland. Most of the routes here are traditional, with a few bolted lines and top-rope options, so bring a rack. Grades cluster in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, with a handful of easier lines and nothing really hard. A 60 meter rope covers the routes and anchors are bolted, though a few finishes need a rappel. Poison oak grows on the cliff and along the trail, so cover up. The south trail from the lot climbs rocky steps straight to this end of the wall.

or_a_picnic_lunch_wall.blurb: Picnic Lunch Wall is the tall cliff rising right above the Crooked River at Smith Rock, a short climb up the stairs past the footbridge. It is mostly bolted sport climbing, with a few trad lines and some aid routes mixed in, and grades run broadly from easy up to the 5.14 range, with the largest group around 5.12 and 5.13. The rock is more fractured than elsewhere in the park, so test holds and wear a helmet. It is a convenient spot when you do not want a long haul with the gear, though the best rock at Smith is generally found elsewhere.

or_main_wall.blurb: Main Wall is the central section of Madrone Wall, a basalt cliff in a county park southeast of Portland. The main trail from the lot leads straight to the middle of it. Routes are mostly traditional with a smaller group of bolted sport lines, with the grades concentrated around 5.10 and 5.11 and a few harder ones near 5.12. Some of the lines are longer than elsewhere on the cliff. A 60 meter rope reaches everything and anchors are bolted, but a few descents involve a rappel. Poison oak is common on the wall and trail, so wear long pants.

or_koala_rock.blurb: Koala Rock is a formation in the Marsupials, the quiet eastern edge of Smith Rock, reached by a long walk from the main lot. It offers a wide spread of grades, from easy 5.4 and 5.5 routes through 5.10 and 5.11 to a couple of 5.12s and 5.13s, mixing sport and trad lines, with a few multi-pitch routes. Many climbs start from a pile of boulders at the base. Because of the distance, crowds are rare and it is a calm place for a day out, and dogs are welcome to tag along. Rock quality varies, so check holds before trusting them.

or_mind_planet.blurb: Mind Planet is one of the most popular crags in the Callahans, a ridge of sandstone cliffs above the Flournoy Valley near Roseburg. The routes are bolted and follow pocketed sandstone, with the climbing concentrated around 5.10 and 5.11 and a few easier and harder lines. Two sections are the main draw, the Near Side with its moderate 5.10s and the steeper Denial Wall. Many lines are two pitches but can be done as a single pitch from the first anchors. Mind Planet sits high on the ridge, so it feels airy, and the rappel from the top is long, so bring a generous rope.
